title: Investigation of Adverse Drug Reactions to Clozapine in Relation to Genotype, Serum Concentration (TDM), Age, Ethnicity, and Gender—CLOVER
summary:
Background: Clozapine is an atypical antipsychotic that is used as the treatment of choice for treatment-resistant schizophrenia [6–8]. However, it is associated with an increased risk of certain serious adverse effects, such as myocarditis and agranulocytosis. Other adverse effects, such as hypersalivation, constipation, and pneumonia, also limit its use.
Research question: Is there a correlation between age, gender, and ethnicity regarding the side effects of clozapine? Can genetic markers be identified that can predict serious side effects?
Methodology: Monitoring of side effects during the titration phase of clozapine using questionnaires. TDM, genetic testing, and lymphocyte transformation test.

interventions.name: Patients who are newly being treated with clozapine for schizophrenia spectrum disorders. A blood sample will be drawn for genotyping. Clinical interviews will be conducted several times. This is a single-arm study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Schizophrenia spectrum disorder, treatment with clozapine
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of legal capacity to consent
